description: NurtureAISpace develops autonomous astronaut health & deep-space nutrition for Mars (Sol-450). Powered by thermodynamic Arrhenius degradation kinetics (NASA JSC calibrated, R²≥0.999), bio-regenerative life support (N-BLSS), and SciPy NASA-STD-3001 diet optimization. Team: Suleyman (Lead Architect), Banu (UI/UX), Yunis (AI/ML), Faruk (Comp Eng). We love space biophysics, AI & aerospace engineering. Open to contributors in astrobiology & space data! Live: https://nurtureaispace.github.io
summary:
NurtureAI Space is health-monitoring software for astronauts on long missions. Every morning an astronaut logs six readings (heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep and mood) in an offline-first phone app. The crew dashboard compares each reading with reference ranges and with that astronaut's own usual values and answers in plain words: All good, Take care, or Call the flight surgeon, plus one next step. A clickable body view shows which area needs attention. The astronaut's name never leaves the phone; only an anonymized code is sent.

Because Mars crews will eat food stored for years, the system also forecasts when vitamins B1, C and D could run low and how much warning the crew gets. In our simulated Mars cooling-failure scenario it warns 43 Sols before a vitamin B1 problem would start.

We tested the personal-baseline idea on real NASA OSDR blood data from the Inspiration4 crew: one day after landing, all four crew members had red-cell size (MCV) below all of their own pre-flight values while still inside the normal lab range, a change a standard check would miss.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
NurtureAI Space helps astronauts check their own health every day and act early.
- Astronaut App (phone, works offline): the astronaut types their name once; it stays on the phone and becomes an anonymized code such as CREW-7F3A2C. Each Sol they log six readings in about 30 seconds. Check-ins are stored on the device and sent automatically when a connection returns, which matters on Mars, where messages to Earth take 4 to 24 minutes.
- Crew dashboard: each crew card shows the six readings with color coding (green, amber, red), a plain status (All good / Take care / Call the flight surgeon) and one next step. A clickable body figure groups readings by area (brain: mood and sleep; heart: heart rate and blood pressure; blood: temperature and blood sugar).
- NASA Evidence: real Inspiration4 blood tests from NASA OSDR (OSD-569, OSD-575). Each person is compared with their own three pre-flight tests. One day after landing, MCV was below all of each person's own pre-flight values in all four crew members, while still inside the 80-100 fL lab range.
- Food & Vitamins: a simulated mission (Earth orbit, Moon or Mars; normal storage or a cooling failure) forecasts when vitamins B1, C and D could run low and how many Sols of warning the crew gets. Mars with a storage failure: warning at Sol 207, problem at Sol 250 (43 Sols early). Orbit and Moon missions are short enough that vitamins last.

HOW IT WORKS
Readings are compared with sourced reference ranges and, after five entries, with the astronaut's personal baseline. Vitamin loss in stored food follows a temperature-dependent (Arrhenius) model, and body vitamin pools are tracked per crew member. Every model parameter and its source is documented in docs/DATA_SOURCES.md and labeled literature, derived or assumed.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT
Early, personal warnings for crews far from a doctor; privacy by design; works without a network. On Earth the same approach fits Antarctic stations, submarines and remote work sites.

TOOLS
Python, FastAPI, pytest; React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS; Progressive Web App (service worker, IndexedDB); GitHub Pages. Source code: https://github.com/NurtureAISpace/mars-food-intelligence

BUILT BEFORE VS DURING THE HACKATHON
Before (Nov 8-13): the original food and vitamin app and the first Crew Health module (see git history and README). During (Nov 14-15): NASA Evidence with Inspiration4 data, literature parameters and the vitamin D model, the daily check-in, the offline Astronaut App with anonymized codes, the redesigned three-screen dashboard, mission destinations, the body view, QR join and the public site.

LIMITATIONS
Inspiration4 has 4 people, 3 baseline tests and a 3-day mission, so it shows the method, not a medical result. The Mars crew and the food catalog items are simulated and labeled as such. Moon and Mars mission lengths are assumptions. The public site shows a demo snapshot; live sync runs in our laptop demo. This is a decision-support prototype, not a medical device.
